title: Katrina Mirpuri Shares Family Diwali Feast Recipes With Tesco for London Homes
excerpt: The journalist known as Curry Bradshaw sets out eight vegetarian family dishes, from potato chaat and saag paneer to tadka daal and salted lassi, with Tesco Clubcard prices running to 10 November 2026.
body:
• Journalist Katrina Mirpuri, known as Curry Bradshaw, has shared eight family Diwali recipes with Tesco and London On The Inside, from potato chaat to tadka daal and salted lassi.
  • The menu is fully vegetarian and built for a home dinner party: saag paneer, bhindi ki sabji, roti, Laila basmati rice and a fresh fruit platter to finish.
  • Tesco Clubcard prices in the guide run to 10 November 2026, including Laila Basmati Rice 10kg at £12.50 (regular £19) and Elephant Atta Chapatti Flour 10kg at £6 (regular £12.50).
  • Mirpuri traces the recipes to her grandmother, saying traditions are passed down through recipes and stories rather than books or temples.

Journalist and party host Katrina Mirpuri has set out how to build a Diwali feast at home, sharing family recipes in a guide produced with Tesco and published by London On The Inside. Mirpuri, who writes as Curry Bradshaw and co-hosted a widely talked-about Diwali party at Broadwick Soho last year, frames the meal as a way of holding on to the people who came before her.

"My grandma taught me so much about our traditions, and those traditions aren't in books or temples - they're in people. Traditions are passed down through recipes and stories."

— Katrina Mirpuri, journalist

The guide arrives ahead of this year's Diwali festivities, when families across London will mark the Festival of Lights with food, volunteering and time together. Mirpuri says giving back is as important as celebrating, whether that means volunteering at the temple, cooking for people or simply spending time together.

The Menu: Eight Dishes Built Around Contrast

The menu opens with potato chaat with chickpeas, pomegranate and clementine, which Mirpuri describes as the best way to wake up taste buds because it is fresh with varied texture. Chickpeas, chopped red onion, coriander, clementines, pomegranate and crushed nuts are layered over boiled potato with yoghurt and served straight away while still crunchy.

Saag paneer follows as a family favourite. Mirpuri says she sometimes makes the paneer from scratch when she has time. In the version in the guide, paneer is fried in Tesco Pure Sunflower Oil until golden, set aside, and then folded back through spinach wilted with garlic and turmeric. Bhindi ki sabji keeps the meal vegetable-forward: okra cooked with mustard seeds, turmeric, cumin and hing, finished with coriander once tender and lightly charred.

Tadka daal provides the comfort course. Yellow moong daal is cooked until soft, then finished with a sizzling tadka of onion and garlic fried with mustard seeds, turmeric and cumin, added at the end so it is still sizzling at the table. Roti made from Elephant Atta Chapatti Flour, Laila basmati rice rinsed until the water runs clear, a salted lassi whisked from plain yoghurt with roasted cumin, and a platter of figs, apples and grapes complete the spread.

What It Costs and Where to Shop

The guide lists Clubcard prices for the staples, with the offer ending 10 November 2026 in the majority of larger stores, Clubcard or app required. Tesco Pure Sunflower Oil 5 litres is listed at a Clubcard price of £6.50, against a regular price of £8.50. The rice and flour offers are larger: Laila Basmati Rice 10kg at £12.50 against £19 regular, and Elephant Atta Medium Chapatti Flour 10kg at £6 against £12.50 regular. Those three staples cover the oil, rice and flour used across the menu.

Tesco has used Diwali recipe guides before to reach the more than 1.5 million people in the UK who celebrate the festival. An earlier Tesco guide reported by Retail Times featured product development chef Neel Shah and mithai such as gulab jamun and barfi, alongside bhel puri and bhajis, with more recipes collected on Tesco Real Food. Mirpuri's menu takes a different route: no mithai course, and a lighter finish of fresh fruit after spiced dishes.

Why the Format Works for Diaspora Kitchens

Every dish in the Mirpuri menu uses a short ingredient list and a single pan or pot, which suits smaller London kitchens and cooks who are hosting after work. The chaat and lassi need no cooking beyond boiling potatoes and whisking yoghurt. The daal and rice can sit covered while the paneer and bhindi are finished. That sequencing is the practical value of the guide: a full festive table without specialist equipment or hard-to-find ingredients, using supermarket staples already stocked for Diwali.

What's Next

Readers who want the full ingredient lists and methods can follow the London On The Inside guide and shop the Clubcard offers before 10 November 2026. For Mirpuri, the point is continuity: cooking her grandmother's dishes for the people at her table now.
